name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
description: A massive text embedding benchmark spanning 8 embedding tasks, covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages, with open-source code, datasets, and a public leaderboard.
creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
citeAs: Muennighoff, Niklas; Tazi, Nouamane; Magne, Loïc; Reimers, Nils. MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark.
rai:dataCollection: MTEB unifies 58 datasets from 8 embedding tasks: bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity, and summarization. It incorporates existing benchmarks such as SemEval datasets (STS11 - STS22) and BEIR alongside other datasets from various tasks. Some datasets were custom-made for MTEB, including ArxivClustering, BiorxivClustering, and MedrxivClustering using public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv; RedditClusteringP2P using available Reddit posts data; and StackExchangeClusteringP2P using available StackExchange posts data. New datasets can be benchmarked by specifying the task and a Hugging Face dataset name where the data has been uploaded.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Software Collection, Document analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include existing public datasets and benchmarks such as SemEval, BEIR, Amazon reviews, Banking77, Emotion, IMDB, MASSIVE, MTOP, Kaggle competition datasets, BUCC, Tatoeba, AskUbuntu, MindSmall, SciDocsRR, StackOverflow duplicate questions, BIOSSES, SICK-R, SummEval, and public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv. RedditClusteringP2P uses available Reddit posts data and StackExchangeClusteringP2P uses available StackExchange posts data.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Several clustering tasks are framed as both sentence-to-sentence and paragraph-to-paragraph tasks; in the latter, titles are concatenated with abstracts or post bodies. For ArxivClustering, abstracts are concatenated to the title in the P2P setting. For arXiv clustering, when multiple categories can be given to a single paper, only the first one is used. For every clustering dataset, split and strategy, subsets of labels are selected and articles are sampled from those labels, yielding splits with varying amounts and sizes of clusters.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MTEB groups datasets into sentence-to-sentence, paragraph-to-paragraph, and sentence-to-paragraph categories. In clustering datasets created for MTEB, S2S inputs use only titles, while P2P inputs concatenate title and abstract or title and post. For classification, train and test sets are embedded and a logistic regression classifier with 100 maximum iterations is trained on train embeddings and scored on test embeddings. For clustering, embedded texts are clustered with mini-batch k-means with batch size 32 and k equal to the number of labels. For pair classification and STS, texts are embedded and compared with distance metrics such as cosine similarity, dot product, euclidean distance, and manhattan distance. For retrieval and reranking, queries and documents/references are embedded and compared using cosine similarity. For summarization, machine-generated summaries are compared to human-written summaries by embedding both and keeping the closest score.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations come from the original source datasets and vary by task. Examples include human-provided category labels for papers in arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv clustering datasets; intent, scenario, sentiment, toxicity, polarity, emotion, and domain labels in classification datasets; duplicate/paraphrase labels in pair classification and reranking datasets; translated sentence pairs in bitext mining datasets; continuous similarity scores in STS datasets; and human assessments of machine-generated summaries in SummEval. For custom clustering datasets from arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv, cluster labels are generated using categories given to the papers by humans.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For pair classification, various distance metrics are evaluated and the best binary threshold is used to compute metrics. For clustering, v-measure is used because it does not depend on cluster label permutation. For summarization, the closest score between a machine summary embedding and all human summary embeddings is kept and used as the model score. The paper notes that parts of SciDocsRR may be included in some models' training data and that controlling for data contamination is challenging; overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets is ignored in MTEB scores.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB provides versioning at a dataset and software level to make results reproducible. JSON files corresponding to all results in the paper have been made available together with the benchmark. MTEB software is open-source, datasets and leaderboard are available on the Hugging Face Hub, and the authors welcome dataset, task, metric, and leaderboard contributions from the community via pull requests and an automatic submission format.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language is explicitly covered, with datasets spanning 112 languages. Some datasets also include user-generated text such as Amazon customer reviews, online banking queries, Twitter messages, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, comments from the Civil Comments platform, and Amazon Alexa utterances.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to make selecting the right embedding model easier and simplify future embedding research and industry applications of text embeddings by providing reliable performance estimates across diverse tasks, efficiency settings, and multilingual scenarios.
rai:dataBiases: MTEB average scores are biased towards tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification and clustering, because tasks have different numbers of datasets. The paper also notes possible data contamination, for example parts of SciDocsRR being included in some models' training data, and states that controlling for overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets is challenging.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark has several stated limitations: it lacks very long document datasets; tasks are imbalanced, with summarization consisting of only a single dataset, biasing average scores toward tasks with many datasets; multilingual coverage is incomplete because retrieval and clustering are English-only; SGPT-BLOOM-7B1-msmarco cannot be comprehensively benchmarked due to lack of multilingual retrieval datasets; MTEB does not contain code datasets; and it focuses solely on natural language applications rather than multimodal downstream uses.
rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is intended for evaluation and benchmarking of text embedding models across 8 tasks and 58 datasets, including English and multilingual subsets. It is used on test splits of all datasets except MSMARCO, where the dev split is used following prior work. It serves as a foundation for comparing models, establishing baselines, selecting embedding models for research or industry applications, and extending evaluation with new datasets, tasks, or metrics.
